findings.evidence: Established pattern: `geodesicBetween_smul` (Geodesic/Between.lean:89), `smul_geodesicLine` (Geodesic.lean:112), `smul_geodesicSegment` (Geodesic/Segment.lean:108), `smul_leftHalfPlane`/`smul_rightHalfPlane` (HalfPlane.lean:134,140), `smul_dirichletDomain` (MeasureTheory/Group/DirichletDomain.lean:169). Polygon/SidePairing.lean:126 already relies on `smul_geodesicSegment` for exactly this kind of step.
findings.fix: Add `bisector_smul (h : PSL(2, ℝ)) {p q : ℍ} (hpq : p ≠ q) : bisector (h • p) (h • q) = h * bisector p q`, from `bisector_def`, `geodesicBetween_smul h hpq`, `(isometry_smul ℍ h).dist_eq` and `mul_assoc`.
findings.issue: `bisector` has no equivariance lemma, unlike every other geodesic-valued construction in the surrounding API. Consumers that push bisectors by group elements (Dirichlet-polygon side pairings, which the PR names as the consumer) can only redo it set-by-set with `ext` plus `dist_smul`.

findings.evidence: `leftHalfPlane_mul_dilation`/`rightHalfPlane_mul_dilation` (HalfPlane.lean:285,295) and `range_geodesicLine_mul_dilation` (Geodesic.lean:204) show each characterized set is unchanged by `* ↑(dilation s)`; `geodesicLine_zero` (Geodesic.lean:107) and `rotation_smul_I` (used at Geodesic.lean:222) give the midpoint lemma in three lines.
findings.fix: Add `geodesicLine_bisector_zero {p q : ℍ} : geodesicLine (bisector p q) 0 = geodesicLine (geodesicBetween p q) (dist p q / 2)` (from `geodesicLine_zero`, `rotation_smul_I`, `geodesicLine_mul_dilation`) and the one-line `mem_leftHalfPlane_bisector_self {p q : ℍ} (hpq : p ≠ q) : p ∈ leftHalfPlane (bisector p q)`.
findings.issue: All five characterizations (lines 122, 131, 138, 145, 151) are invariant under `bisector p q * ↑(dilation s)`, so the API cannot distinguish `bisector p q` from any reparametrization of it. The basepoint and orientation content asserted in the docstrings — "moving to the midpoint of the oriented segment" (line 50) and "its left half-plane contains `p`" (line 45) — is stated nowhere as a lemma, so no equation about the element is provable without re-unfolding `bisector_def` and redoing the rotation/dilation computation.

findings.evidence: Both are true and immediate: `mem_leftHalfPlane_bisector_iff hpq.symm z` gives `dist z q < dist z p`, which is `mem_rightHalfPlane_bisector_iff hpq z`; likewise `mem_range_geodesicLine_bisector_iff` on both sides differ only by `eq_comm`.
findings.fix: Add `leftHalfPlane_bisector_comm {p q : ℍ} (hpq : p ≠ q) : leftHalfPlane (bisector q p) = rightHalfPlane (bisector p q)` and `range_geodesicLine_bisector_comm : range (geodesicLine (bisector q p)) = range (geodesicLine (bisector p q))`, each by `ext` plus the existing `mem_*_bisector_iff` lemmas.
findings.issue: Same class of gap: no lemma relates `bisector q p` to `bisector p q`, although the file deliberately develops both sides (left and right, open and closed). The Dirichlet-polygon pairing of the side for `g` with the side for `g⁻¹` needs exactly this.

summary: The rename is clean and the half-plane membership characterizations are right, but `bisector` is a new `PSL(2, ℝ)`-valued definition with no group-element-level API: no equivariance, no basepoint lemma, no swap relation, so nothing in the API pins it down beyond right multiplication by a dilation.
